```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown

from rse_survey_report.book import BOOK_CATEGORIES, BOOK_DIR, load_book_data
from rse_survey_report.config import NORDICS
from rse_survey_report.freetext import (
    TEXT_TYPES,
    allocate_tokens,
    question_tokens,
    summarize_allocation,
)
from rse_survey_report.plotting import (
    GROUP_COLORS,
    plot_agreement,
    plot_bool,
    plot_choice,
    plot_likert2,
)
from rse_survey_report.recode_maps import RECODE_MAPS
from rse_survey_report.utils import get_data_path, load_data, preprocess_data

codebook, df, df_compare = load_book_data()

df_all = preprocess_data(
    load_data(get_data_path("2026_tf.csv", 2026)), excl_var="submitdate_0"
)
df_submitted = df_all[df_all["complete"]]

n_rows = len(df_all)
n_submitted = len(df_submitted)
n_countries = df_submitted["country"].nunique()
n_nordic = len(df)
n_chapters = len(list((BOOK_DIR / "chapters").glob("*.qmd")))

PLUM = "#822361"


def n_answered(question: str) -> int:
    """Count the respondents with a free-text answer to a question."""
    rows = codebook[(codebook["id"] == question) & codebook["type"].isin(TEXT_TYPES)]
    return int(df[rows["col"].unique()].notna().any(axis=1).sum())


def free_text_bars(question: str, top: int = 8):
    """Plot the largest free-text categories of a question."""
    tokens = question_tokens(df, codebook, question)
    rules = RECODE_MAPS.get(question, [])
    counts = summarize_allocation(allocate_tokens(tokens, rules)).head(top)
    # reversed order puts the largest bar at the top of a horizontal chart
    fig = px.bar(
        counts.iloc[::-1],
        x="n",
        y="category",
        orientation="h",
        text="n",
        color_discrete_sequence=[PLUM],
        labels={"n": "Answer parts", "category": ""},
        height=420,
    )
    fig.update_layout(plot_bgcolor="white")
    return fig
```

# Method: background

## A Quarto book as a complement to the dashboard

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Dashboard**

- [Link to dashboard](https://rse-survey.soton.ac.uk/superset/dashboard/RSE_survey/)
- Interactive dashboard for international RSE survey data
- Focus: explorative data analysis
- Interactive filters and cross-filters
- All countries in one place
- Fast answers to ad-hoc questions

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Quarto book** (new)

- [Lives in GitHub](https://github.com/nordic-rse/rse-survey-2026/pull/15)
- One question at a time, with its question text
- Ready to share: meetings, reports, appendices
- Custom analysis, groups, visualisations, etc.
- Reproducible, Open source, Python 3.x
:::
::::

## Structure of the book

**Folder structure**

```text
data/2026/             survey CSV files (not in git)
src/rse_survey_report/
  config.py            Nordics, groups, topics
  codebook.py          question type, answers, order
  plotting.py          plot_choice, plot_agreement, ...
  book.py              writes one chapter per question
book/
  _setup.qmd           loads the data for each chapter
  chapters/            generated chapters
Makefile               make book, make slides, make test
```

**Contents**

- `{python} n_chapters` chapters, one for each question.
- Current template for chapters has four sections:
  - **Nordics**, **By age group**, **Within Nordics**, **Between countries**

## Use the book for your own analysis

| Task | Edit | Then run |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Render the book | Put the CSV files in `data/2026/` | `make book` |
| Change a plot | A function in `plotting.py` | `make test`, then `make book` |
| Change a group | `AGE_GROUPS` or `COMPARE_GROUPS` in `config.py` | `make book` |
| Add a section to each chapter | `chapter_qmd()` in `book.py` | `make book` |

- `make book` writes the chapters again and renders it to `book/_book/`.

## How to go further with the book (I)

::: {.callout-warning}
The book is under active development. Its structure can still change.
:::

**Flexibility**

- Make the analysis easier to customize, with more modular code
- Change the target and comparison countries without editing code
- Offer alternative visualizations

**Data**

- Add earlier survey waves, with a section that compares the years
- Show connections between questions

## How to go further with the book (II)

**Free text**

- Analyse free-text answers faster: cluster and label them with NLP and local language models

**Community**

- Link the book and the dashboard clearly
- Work with the survey team to keep the book useful for all countries and future years
- Collect requirements: which template structure, and which ready-made analyses users can select

**Documentation**

- Write tutorials and how-to guides for the book

## Nordics: respondents per question

Country-specific questions have few or no Nordic responses.

```{python}
col_to_id = (
    codebook[codebook["col"].isin(df.columns)]
    .drop_duplicates("col")
    .set_index("col")["id"]
)
answered = df[col_to_id.index].notna().T.groupby(col_to_id, sort=False).any().T
answered = answered.loc[:, answered.any()]
per_country = (
    answered.groupby(df["country"])
    .sum()
    .reindex(NORDICS, fill_value=0)
    .T.reset_index(names="question")
    .melt(id_vars="question", var_name="country", value_name="respondents")
)
fig = px.bar(
    per_country,
    x="question",
    y="respondents",
    color="country",
    category_orders={"country": NORDICS, "question": list(answered.columns)},
    color_discrete_sequence=GROUP_COLORS,
    labels={"question": "Question id", "respondents": "Respondents", "country": ""},
    height=480,
)
fig.update_layout(plot_bgcolor="white", xaxis_tickangle=-90, xaxis_dtick=1)
fig.update_xaxes(tickfont_size=8)
fig.show()
```

## Discussion

- **Survey activity.** Did you answer the survey? If not, why?
- **Social sciences.** Minority of RSEs work in social sciences and majority in computer sciences.
  Are there few RSEs in social sciences and psychology, or did the survey not reach them?
  How can Nordic-RSE reach out to these fields?
- **Other activities.** Respondents want to spend less time on "other activities".
  Besides research, software development, teaching and management: what else takes your time?
- **Labour market.** 16% disagree that their experience is in demand.
  Which skills or experience are missing to succeed on the job market?
- **Promotion.** Promotion routes seem unclear.
  What is your experience? What would make the routes clearer?
- **DOIs for software.** 20 of 25 respondents never create a DOI for their software.
  Why not? Is it not relevant for your software, or did you not know it is possible?
